payload.title: Mon 9/28: What a craving is trying to say
payload.purpose: A craving as information, not a failure. Mindful Eating and Coping Skills from the Behavioral Therapy & Counseling pillar, in plain words.

captions.FB:
A craving isn't a failure. It's information.

When you feel a strong urge to eat, your body or mind is trying to tell you something. Maybe you're truly hungry. Maybe you're stressed, tired, or lonely. Maybe a certain food is tied to a memory or a feeling of comfort.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we teach clients to pause and ask: What is this craving really about?

That question is at the heart of Mindful Eating and Coping Skills, part of our Behavioral Therapy & Counseling pillar. We help people understand and modify their relationship with food, not through rules or restriction, but through awareness and compassion.

Our program includes group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

payload.title: Tue 11/3: Referring providers: what comes back to you
payload.purpose: Coordination with the referring provider and the discharge summary of behavioral progress (assessment scores: nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, depression). LinkedIn document post, Todd's sentences verbatim.

captions.LI:
When you refer a patient to the Bariatric Counseling Center, you receive consistent coordination throughout their care and a detailed discharge summary at program completion.

Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We accept most health insurances.

San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

payload.title: Tue 11/10: Referring providers: who is the right referral
payload.purpose: Standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medication. Pre and post bariatric patients in one bullet.

captions.LI:
The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients seeking standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, as well as those receiving bariatric surgery or weight loss medications from their medical providers.

Our intensive outpatient program supports pre-surgical and post-surgical bariatric patients. We coordinate care with referring providers and deliver detailed discharge summaries of behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

We accept most health insurances. Claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits. Patients typically attend for little to no cost.

Serving patients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

At discharge, we deliver detailed summaries of patient behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression. Progress notes as requested, typically within two business days.
